documents.title: Sickle Cell Clinic Letter
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Adult Sickle Cell Program
Visit 03/13/2023

Brief update for his primary care physician. Darnell continues to do well on hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily with folic acid and penicillin prophylaxis. No admissions over the past year. Counts reviewed at today's visit and at his steady state. No change to his regimen. We will see him again in six months.

Adult Sickle Cell Program

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
23 y/o with HbSS here for his yearly exam.
Good year. No ED visits or admissions. Hematology letter from March: stable, same regimen. Working more hours at the library this summer. Hip: some days worse than others, no rest pain, not waking him up.
Meds: hydroxyurea 1000 daily, folic acid 1 mg daily (uses the alarm), penicillin VK 250 BID. NKDA.
No tobacco or vaping. Alcohol rarely.
ROS: negative except the hip.
Exam: lean, comfortable. HEENT unremarkable. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft, spleen tip at the costal margin, no tenderness. R hip end-range IR pain, unchanged. Skin without ulcers.
PHQ-2 1.
A/P
- HbSS: steady. Annual CBC, CMP, urine albumin.
- Splenomegaly: small, stable on exam.
- R femoral head AVN: stable symptoms; he knows to call ortho back if he gets rest pain or a new limp.
- Health maintenance: vaccines current for asplenia, MenACWY next due 2026. Flu/COVID in fall.
See in 6 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs from yesterday look like you: hemoglobin around 9, kidneys normal, no protein in the urine, liver tests fine. Nothing to do. Enjoy the long library hours.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Influenza (R) and 2023-24 COVID (L) given. Denies illness today. No reaction during the observation period.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Sickle Cell Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six-month visit. No pain episodes needing care since early 2020. Saw hematology in September, unchanged. Folic acid refills running low, will send. Penicillin from hematology.
Thinks about the hip more in the cold. Stays warm, carries water.
Exam: well, comfortable. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, spleen tip palpable, nontender.
A/P: HbSS, doing well. Folic acid refilled for a year. Labs due with his physical in June. Fever plan reviewed for the winter.

documents.title: Folic acid
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Pharmacy says they only got 30 days on the folic acid not the year. Can you check?

documents.title: RE: Folic acid
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Sorry about that, the refills did not go through with the first script. Resent 90 days with 3 refills just now. Should be ready this afternoon.

documents.title: Letter for school
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, the disability services office at school needs a letter that I have sickle cell so I can have water in class and miss without penalty if I'm in the hospital. Can you do that?

documents.title: Letter - Medical Accommodation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
To Disability Services:

Darnell Grant is a patient of this practice with sickle cell disease, a lifelong condition. Episodes of severe pain can occur without warning and may require emergency care or hospitalization. Staying hydrated and warm lowers that risk.

Please allow him to keep water with him in class and to take restroom breaks as needed, to dress for warmth in cold rooms, and to make up work or exams missed for medical care.

Please contact our office with questions.

Primary Care Physician

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Feels well. School letter went through in January. No crises, no ED. Hematology every 6 months, last in March, no changes. R hip ache stable.
Meds: hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, penicillin VK 250 mg BID. NKDA.
SH unchanged: library job, classes, lives with family. Never smoker. Alcohol rare.
ROS negative.
Exam: well. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, spleen tip palpable. R hip as before. No edema. Skin clear.
PHQ-2 0.
A/P: HbSS, stable on hematology's regimen. Labs today. Eye exam due again (last 8/2022) - he will call the eye office himself. Vaccines up to date; flu/COVID in October. Six-month check by video in late summer if he prefers.

documents.title: Your labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Darnell, your yearly labs are stable: hemoglobin near 9, white count at your usual, kidney function and urine protein normal. Talk soon.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit - Sickle Cell Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit from his break room at work, two identifiers confirmed.
No pain crises. Energy fine. Taking all three meds. Fall semester starts next week; has his accommodation letter on file with school.
No fever, chest pain, breathing trouble.
Observation on video: well appearing, speaking full sentences, no distress.
A/P: HbSS stable. Reminded about the eye exam, he has not scheduled it yet. Flu and COVID in October at a nurse visit. Next in-person visit in the spring.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: 2024-25 flu (R arm) and COVID (L arm). No acute complaints, afebrile by report. Stayed 15 minutes, left feeling fine.
